data.gender_notes: Samritaan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Samritaan is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word 'samriddh', meaning prosperous or wealth. The name Samritaan is associated with the Hindu goddess of prosperity, Lakshmi. It is a rare and beautiful name that is sure to bring good fortune and happiness to any child. The name Samritaan carries the meaning “Goddess of Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Samritaan usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Samritaan is a name that signifies the divine presence of the goddess Lakshmi, the Hindu deity of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. It is believed that invoking the name Samritaan will bring abundance and happiness into one's life.
data.etymology: Samritaan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samritaan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Samritaan is a tribute to the rich cultural heritage of Hinduism. The name carries the spiritual essence of the gods and goddesses that are revered in this ancient tradition. Venerating the goddess of prosperity, Lakshmi, with the name is a nod to the importance of abundance, prosperity, and wealth in Hindu culture and spirituality.
data.spiritual_significance: Samritaan is a name that holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is believed that by giving a child this name, the goddess of prosperity, Lakshmi, will bless the child with an abundance of material wealth, happiness, and good fortune. Additionally, the name Samritaan serves as a daily reminder of the importance of seeking prosperity not just in material terms but also in spiritual terms. Through this name, parents hope to instill a sense of gratitude, generosity, and contentment in their child, knowing that true wealth lies in the heart and in the blessings of the gods.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Samritaan is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Sam' (together) and 'Ritaan' (rules). It symbolizes one who upholds dharma, or cosmic order, in unity and harmony within themselves and their community.

historical_references.reference: Samritaan was a famous Jaina monk and scholar during the Gupta Empire in the 5th century CE. He was a disciple of Haribhadra Suri and is known for his commentary on the 'Yogavasisha' of Haribhadra Suri, which is a seminal work on Jaina ascetic practices and Yoga.

historical_references.reference: Samritaan is also mentioned in the 'Prabandha-Chintamani' of Hemacandra, a 12th century Jaina scholar. He is listed among the great Jaina scholars of the Bhagavati sect and is known for his works on Jaina logic, metaphysics, and grammar.
